issue_context.title: "inject" doesn't respond when async route doesn't have a return statement
issue_context.body:
### Prerequisites

- [X] I have written a descriptive issue title
- [X] I have searched existing issues to ensure the bug has not already been reported


### Fastify version

4.5.2

### Plugin version

_No response_

### Node.js version

16.16

### Operating system

Linux

### Operating system version (i.e. 20.04, 11.3, 10)

5.15.60-1-MANJARO

### Description

We've captured this issue while testing our async routes which don't have a `return` statement:

- Browser behavior is normal when accessing the route;
- `inject` method hangs while awaiting a response from the route;

### Steps to Reproduce

Create a Fastify server with a `GET` route to "/" with no `return` statement.

```
function buildServer() {
  const fastify = require('fastify')()
  fastify.get('/', async function (request, reply) {})
  return fastify
}
```

- Build the server and notice how the route works in the Browser;

```
const server = buildServer()
server.listen({ port: 3000 })
```

- Invoke `inject` for the route;

```
async function testInject() {
  const response = await server.inject({
    method: 'GET',
    url: '/'
  })

  console.log("expecting a response", response);
}
```

Notice how `console.log` is not reached, and the server hangs.



### Expected Behavior

If we omit `return` (or `reply.send({})`) the Browser still responds. But `inject` hangs.
We'd like to `inject` to have the same behavior as the browser, then we would be able to create async routes without `return` statements and/or non-async routes with no `reply.send({})` statements.
comments: I'll be taking a look at this issue.

> then we would be able to create async routes without return statements and/or non-async routes with no reply.send({}) statements.

what is the expected result?

> We'd like to inject to have the same behavior as the browser

Could you elaborate?

> > then we would be able to create async routes without return statements and/or non-async routes with no reply.send({}) statements.
> 
> what is the expected result?
**The expected result is for jest or node-tap to not hang when testing routes without return statements**
 
> > We'd like to inject to have the same behavior as the browser
> 
> Could you elaborate?
**Ideally, inject should return a response after it receives an undefined body from a route handler**
Thanks for reporting! Would you like to send a Pull Request to address this issue? Remember to add unit tests.
Handlers need to return something, see https://www.fastify.io/docs/latest/Guides/Migration-Guide-V4/#need-to-return-reply-to-signal-a-fork-of-the-promise-chain
That's technically not true, if they return nothing it's an empty http response.

> That's technically not true, if they return nothing it's an empty http response.

But I mean, don't they still have to return an empty response? I.e.:

```js
fastify.get('/sync', function (request, reply) { reply.send()})
fastify.get('/async', async function (request, reply) { return ''})
```

I must say that the docs are a little confusing in this regard, but in any case, what we noticed (which is what's described in the issue) is that it works in the browser, whereas fastify.inject hangs. So, I assume there must be something that fastify.inject does that doesn't match what a real HTTP client does

I can confirm this is indeed a problem with inject. There is an [existing test](https://github.com/simoneb/fastify/blob/ba45196eb4c442ae911b28deeca1905e676a726e/test/async-await.test.js#L386) confirming that this scenario works with a plain HTTP client in the codebase. 

I added a test which is doing the same thing with .inject and it fails. I don't have a solution atm, but at least there's a repro. 

https://github.com/fastify/fastify/pull/4211
I tracked down the issue to an `aborted` property not being set in the request object created by light-my-request. Opened issue https://github.com/fastify/light-my-request/issues/217 there

@mcollina with light-my-request's new release you did a few minutes ago, bumping that package's version here will fix the issue. Do we bump it explicitly in https://github.com/fastify/fastify/pull/4211 by changing the light-my-request version or do we just leave npm to do its job and bump it on the next npm install? Asking because I see the semver specifier is quite loose (^5.0.0 although light-my-request is now at 5.5.1)
Meanwhile, I bumped the light-my-request version and opened the PR for review https://github.com/fastify/fastify/pull/4211
The bug still exists in Version 4.24.0

This issue is +1 year old.

Please open a new detailed issue adding a [Minimal, Reproducible Example](https://stackoverflow.com/help/minimal-reproducible-example).
